questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had never been to Australia, but I'd always wanted to go. Because of the distance I always felt that you needed atleast a few months to go there, which was never an option until I started studying and exchange became a possibility. On top of that, the University of Melbourne is highly regarded internationally, and I was curious to experience a different approach to the psychology degree. 
On top of that it is an english speaking country, and Melbourne is very similiar to European cities culturally, politically etc. 
... And I also just really wanted to travel around Australia, which was possible during the stay, where I visited Tasmania and various locations around Victoria during the exchange and travelled the east coast of Australia for a month upon its completion.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty straightforward, and the host university was very helpful. That being said, I did have some difficulty locating the right subjects/courses, and the University of Melbourne turned out to be very "square" with regards to the psychology degree, where it was impossible to find courses on clinical psychology as an undergraduate. Also there were alot of people wanting help, so you did have to wait for quite a bit before they got back to you.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received some assistance regarding course planning, but not really for anything else.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was very hard. Melbourne is going through an accommodation crisis, and there was a lot of competition for available appartments/rooms. I was VERY lucky that I found a room, as I've heard that a lot of people looked for weeks and months without any luck.
I can really recommend spending a lot of time looking before arriving, and making sure to write very personalized e-mails to people putting up an add.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
The center of Melbourne (CBD) is very busy and full of everything you need, but I'd say the suburbs are much preferable. Make sure to chose one close to the CBD as it is a very big city and transportation is both expensive and time consuming. 
I was in Footscray, which was very similar to Nordvest in Copenhagen and around 30 minutes away from Campus and 15 away from Flinders Street station, which is in the center of the city. Fitzroy, Carlton, Parkville, Melbourne North, Docklands etc would also be good locations.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Campus housing was VERY expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I felt that there was a lot on information, deadlines and various different pages where one needed to sign up, which was a bit complicated.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I can't really remember.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to write them regarding difficulties with this process, but I found that they took a long time getting back to you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had a hard time finding substitutes for the classes at my home university. Clinical Psychology (bachelor) was impossible, but I did manage to find substitutes for my elective/valgfag and Forskningsdesign og Videnskabs teori.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just make sure you have some time to really read the information and become familiarized with the different platforms.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought they had some very interesting courses, but that they were often quite superficial.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did Undergraduate 3 and an Honours course as a fifth/sixth semester student in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite similar with lectures and classes in most of the subjects.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Trauma, Memory, Bodies/The Psychopathology of Everyday Life and The History and Philosophy of Science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked them all, but I'm not really sure I would recommend them.

questions.answer: Everything was really expensive, which was a bit unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I didn't spend any money on books, which was a nice change.
Food, transport and accomodation turned out to be very expensive.
Activites were expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: University of Melbourne has a LOT of clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much everything. I was a member of the Mountaineering and Scuba Diving clubs, which was great

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both of the above if you are into hiking or diving.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I can recommend just walking around the city and exploring the suburbs. 
If you are into hiking, I really loved the Dandenong Ranges and the beach walk between Brighton and St. Kilda. 
I loved the Great Ocean Road, The Grampians (nationalpark) and Wilsons Promotory (nationalpark) for hikes and wildlife. I also really liked the towns of Bright and Castlemaine.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy - they are quite similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
I found it quite hard to meet locals in Melbourne. As with any big city the residents are quite busy and most of them already have a network of friends, and don't neccessarily want to spend time with someone who is only there for a few months. 
You have to be very open and make an effort to meet them. I used the app MeetUp quite a bit, and found a lot of groups where I met some very nice people. 
I can also recommend wednesday boardgames at Fortress in CBD, as a good place to meet cool people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians (overall) are very chill and laid back, and they have a great sense of humour.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be ready to put in a lot of time to make the exchange happen
Don't just hang out with the other danish or international students, but make an effort to socialize
Don't stay in campus housing
Don't spend all your time on school, but explore the city and the surrounds - it is very beautiful down there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring Australia - it is a spectacular place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Bureaucracy and housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
